info.title: QueueFlow API
info.description: REST API for QueueFlow, a PostgreSQL-native distributed job queue and workflow engine.

count is an extra full scan over the filtered set).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque keyset cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`. When set,
`offset` is ignored and listing continues where that page ended.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description:
Only rows created at or after this instant (RFC 3339, inclusive).
With `created_before` this forms the half-open range `[after, before)`
— the natural shape for walking history period by period.

get.summary:
Stream a job's status transitions as Server-Sent Events until it reaches a
terminal state. Lets clients await completion without polling the REST
endpoint themselves.

BackoffStrategy.description: How retry delays grow between attempts.

lease_token.description: The lease token returned by the lease call.

result.description: Handler result, recorded on the job and merged into workflow context.

CreateCronRequest.description: Request body for creating a cron schedule.

cron_expr.description: 5-field crontab (UTC); 6/7 fields with leading seconds also accepted.

payload.description: Arbitrary JSON object passed to the handler.

run_at.description:
Don't run before this instant (RFC 3339). The job is created
immediately but stays invisible to workers until then.

task_name.description: The registered task handler to invoke.

CreateWorkflowRequest.description:
Request body for creating a workflow. Shared by the builder DSL and the API
so callers and SDKs use the same contract.

CronSchedule.description:
A recurring enqueue schedule. Expressions are standard 5-field crontab
(`minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`), evaluated in **UTC**; a
6/7-field form with leading seconds is also accepted.

next_run_at.description:
The next instant this schedule fires. Missed occurrences (server
down) collapse into at most one catch-up firing.

queue_name.description: Queue for the enqueued jobs (the engine default when absent).

DeadLetter.description:
A dead-lettered job: a terminal failure recorded for inspection and
replay. The original job row remains (subject to retention); this entry
captures why it died and, once replayed, which fresh job took its place.

replay_job_id.description: The fresh job created by the replay.

replayed_at.description:
Set once this entry has been replayed; a dead letter replays at most
once.

lease_token.description: The lease token returned by the lease call.

retryable.description:
Whether the engine may retry (subject to the job's max_retries).
Defaults to true; send false for permanent failures (e.g. bad input).

extend_secs.description: New lease duration in seconds, measured from now (1..=3600).

lease_token.description: The lease token returned by the lease call.

delivery_count.description:
How many times this job has been claimed (delivered to a worker).
Greater than `retry_count + 1` means a lease expired without a report —
i.e. a worker crashed mid-run.

idempotency_key.description:
Client-supplied key that makes job creation idempotent per tenant:
re-submitting the same key returns the original job instead of creating
a duplicate.

next_retry_at.description:
When this job's next retry becomes claimable (mirrors `scheduled_at`
while the job is `retrying`; kept for audit/inspection).

scheduled_at.description:
When the job becomes claimable. `created_at` for immediate jobs, the
requested `run_at` for scheduled jobs, and the next backoff instant
while retrying — the durable delay lives in the row itself.

workflow_step_id.description: The owning workflow step's name (steps are addressed by name).

JobConfig.description:
Per-job execution configuration. All durations are in seconds.

Deserialization is partial-friendly: any omitted field takes its
[`JobConfig::default`] value (via per-field serde defaults), so
workflow-step and cron config overrides can name just the fields they
change, and out-of-band rows with sparse `config` JSONB still load.
Per-field functions rather than a struct-level `#[serde(default)]`:
the struct-level form makes utoipa attach a `default` beside the
`BackoffStrategy` `$ref`, which forces a synthetic wrapper type into
every generated SDK.

jitter_factor.description:
Optional jitter in `0.0..=1.0`. `0.1` => +/-10% randomization of each
retry delay, which spreads out thundering-herd retries.

priority.description:
Higher is claimed first within a queue; ties break on `scheduled_at`,
then `created_at`.
Higher is claimed first within a queue (ties: oldest first).

oneOf.description: How retry delays grow between attempts (default exponential).

retry_max_delay_secs.description: Upper bound on any computed retry delay, in seconds.

JobStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a single job.

lease_secs.description: Lease duration in seconds (1..=3600, default 30). Heartbeat to extend.

max_jobs.description: Maximum jobs to lease in one call (1..=100, default 1).

wait_secs.description: Long-poll wait when the queue is empty, in seconds (0..=30, default 0).

LeasedJob.description:
A job leased to a (possibly remote) worker, together with the lease token
needed to heartbeat, complete, or fail it.

lease_token.description:
Opaque, unguessable proof of lease ownership, regenerated on every
claim. Pass it back on heartbeat/complete/fail; a stale token (the
lease expired and the job was reclaimed) is rejected.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque keyset cursor for the next page (present when `has_more`).
Pass it back as `cursor` to continue where this page ended; cheaper
than deep OFFSET paging.

total.description: Exact total match count; only present when `include_total=true`.

than deep OFFSET paging.

than deep OFFSET paging.

Pass it back as `cursor` to continue where this page ended; cheaper
than deep OFFSET paging.

OnFailure.description: What to do with downstream steps when a step fails.

OnSuccess.description: Reserved for future expansion; only `Continue` is meaningful today.

job_id.description: The fresh job created from the dead-lettered one.

StepStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a single workflow step.

Workflow.description: A workflow instance and its steps.

context.description:
Accumulated step results, keyed by step name. Passed to downstream steps
under the `_context` payload key.

WorkflowStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a workflow instance.

WorkflowStep.description:
A node in a workflow DAG. Steps are addressed by their unique `name`;
`depends_on` lists the names of steps that must complete first.

WorkflowStepState.description: Runtime status of one workflow step (the live progress view).

job_id.description: The job executing this step, once one has been scheduled.

name.description: The step's name (its address within the workflow).

steps.description: One entry per step, in declaration order.
